claims.statement: app/globals.css is the single runtime style entrypoint: it imports Tailwind v4 and the layout-only app/design-system.css, then defines the :root token block copied verbatim from docs/design/colors_and_type.css, which the file's own header designates the source of truth for color; app/design-system.css contains only layout/component classes (shell, sidebar, topbar, buttons, focus, data rows, keyframes) that reference token variables, and tremor chart utilities are bridged via @config scoped to the analytics module.

IBM Plex Sans (300-600) and IBM Plex Mono (300-500) are self-hosted with next/font in app/layout.tsx, exposing --font-ibm-plex-sans/--font-ibm-plex-mono on <html>, and :root in app/globals.css prepends those variables to --font-sans/--font-mono so the optimized layout-shift-free fonts win with system names as fallbacks; Inter/Geist/Roboto/Arial are banned as primary typefaces.

The color system is six semantic hues (blue informational/TWSP, teal CFSP, green completed/approved/on-track, amber warning 7-21 days, red critical <7 days/errors, purple NC levels) each with staged tokens (base/-lt/-dk/-border/-hover), and every color carries exactly one meaning; the urgency tier (critical <=6 days, warning 7-21, on-track >21) is computed once at data fetch and stored on the batch - daysUntil() returns Infinity for a missing deadline so absent dates never trigger urgency tiers.

Documented deviations (marked in DESIGN.md, which win over the spec): amber and red hex values were re-tinted warmer/more vivid, and the spec's 3px colored left border was removed from BatchCards, InfoCallouts (now a 1px tinted full-perimeter border), and warning/critical MetricCards (now a tinted label icon and sub-label), with urgency instead communicated by the header badge and the billing-deadline value color.

The primary icon system, shared/ui/Icon.tsx, renders an inline map of Tabler 2px-stroke SVG path strings with currentColor inheritance and aria-hidden, ported verbatim from the design handoff to keep glyphs pixel-identical and avoid a runtime dependency; it is pure render and safe in both Server and Client trees. @tabler/icons-react is declared in package.json as the spec-canonical library, and the only current direct importer is modules/auth/ui/SignUpModal.tsx.

No emoji are allowed anywhere in the UI (and no Unicode glyph or PNG icons); UI copy follows the administrative voice rules: no exclamation marks, no we/you, Title Case for data-system nouns (Batch, Scholar, NTP, BSRS, NC II), sentence case for buttons/labels, and units always included with numbers.

Status is conveyed by text plus icon, never color alone, targeting WCAG 2.2 AA (the upstream spec sheet states WCAG 2.1 AA; the repo rule is the stricter target). This is enforced structurally: the focus-visible ring (2px blue, 2px offset) was added because the ported stylesheet had no focus rule at all, and billing-queue row selection is announced structurally via aria-selected, never by tint alone.

Component layering is app route Server Component -> modules/<domain>/ui screens -> shared/ui props-only primitives: routes are thin (fetch via a module's data/, compose module UI), another module's data/ is private with only app/ able to fetch it, shared/ can never import modules/ or app/, and raw DB types from lib/supabase/database.types.ts are restricted to data layers - all enforced by import/no-restricted-paths in eslint.config.mjs. If a shared/ui component starts reading data or encoding business rules, it must be moved into its owning module.

Components default to Server Components with client islands only for interactivity: BatchCard is 'use client' for hover elevation and opening BatchModal, Sidebar is 'use client' for pathname/drawer/tenant state, while the dashboard layout and page are Server Components.

Existing primitives (BatchCard, BatchModal, StatusBadge, LifecyclePipeline, EmptyState, InfoCallout, etc.) must be reused rather than creating parallels; CardsView and TableView both compose the same BatchCard/BatchModal/StatusBadge/EmptyState set, differing only in arrangement.

Every data screen must implement all six mandatory states - loading, empty, no-results, error/sync-failed, permission-denied, stale-data - and screens with relative dates must show an exact 'Data as of' timestamp (RULES.md section 4, rule 24).

State derivation works through discriminated snapshots: getBatchesSnapshot() (cache-wrapped so the dashboard layout and its nested page share one Supabase query per request) returns BatchesSnapshot of ok / sync-failed / unconfigured, and selectBatchesForDisplay() returns rows only on ok — neither unconfigured (no Supabase env) nor sync-failed (configured but errored) substitutes mock or fabricated data (shared/mocks/ was removed in the mock-data retirement, RULES 2.16), so both render an honest empty state, and sync-failed must additionally surface the sync-failed banner with Retry (RULES 3.19). The dashboard additionally supports a ?state= preview override; denied is preview-only until the tenant/role resolver (TES-34), and stale derives from real data freshness — the freshest row's updated_at older than the 24h DATA_STALE_AFTER_MS threshold.

The 'Data as of' stamp is formatted from the freshest live updated_at (resolveDataAsOfDate returns a Date only for an ok snapshot carrying dataAsOf) as e.g. 'Jun 19, 2026 · 14:02' using hourCycle h23 (midnight prints 00:02, never 24:02), and degrades to the literal 'unknown' (DATA_AS_OF_FALLBACK in DashboardHeader) whenever there is no real timestamp to read, rather than printing a fake precise timestamp; BillingQueueView receives its dataAsOf as an explicit prop stamped as 'Packet readiness · Data as of {dataAsOf}' (plus ' · STALE'), and the billing route's formatAsOf degrades to a fixed fallback date when no row carries an updated_at.
UI copy must never imply official TESDA approval or submission: the app is an internal working layer and TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS remain authoritative (RULES.md section 5, rule 27).

assets/, preview/, screenshots/, ui_kits/, and uploads/ are ported verbatim from the design bundle, excluded from lint and build (eslint.config.mjs globalIgnores), and a PreToolUse hook enforces the rule at [hook] level; the committed script .claude/hooks/protect-static-dirs.sh exits non-zero on edits under those directories with the instruction to edit the source design files first, and public/assets/ is explicitly exempt as the app's real runtime static directory. Hook registration in .claude/settings.json is per-machine gitignored state — only .claude/hooks/ and .claude/agents/ are committed. FIGMA FILES/, diagrams/, and .design-sync/ are review-level design artifacts, and FIGMA FILES/ and .design-sync/ are not materialized in the committed tree — Figma pages are referenced by node ID in code comments.

The design-sync workflow makes the local Next.js TypeScript components the implementation layer, ported verbatim from the handoff JSX in ui_kits/admin/ (each ported component carries a 'ported from components/X.jsx' header); when spec and deviation conflict the deviation wins and colors_and_type.css plus ui_kits/admin/ are the live ground truth, so design changes go to the source design files first. The .design-sync/ directory is gitignored local tooling (not committed) that records the design-project mapping on the machine that holds it.

The shell MetricsRow enforces compliance-copy invariants against false alarms: the hasBatches guard is load-bearing (TES-74) so an empty batch set is never styled as a critical red billing deadline, and 'All verified' must not appear when there is nothing to verify (unknown, not cleared, per ADR-004).

The dashboard maps the snapshot to its six states through named render-derivation helpers — resolveDataAsOfDate(), dataAsOfLabelFor()/formatDataStamp(), isEmptyDashboard(), isSyncFailedDashboard(), isStaleDashboard(), and syncFailedMessageFor() — folded by deriveDashboardViewState(forcedState, snapshot, batchCount) into a DashboardViewState of { isDenied, isEmpty, syncFailed, isStale, dataAsOfLabel, syncFailedMessage }; the guard-clause order in DashboardPage is trusted-lookup failure, trainer redirect, denied, syncFailed && zero rows, empty, then content, so a real sync failure (which yields zero batches with no mock fallback) always reads as a failure with its retry banner, never as an empty tenant — the ordering hazard RULES 3.19 calls out explicitly.

resolveTrustedDashboardRole() reads only the trusted Clerk publicMetadata role (never ?role=) and distinguishes 'lookup succeeded, no role set' (least-privilege viewer display fallback) from 'the lookup itself errored' (getCurrentUser threw); on lookup-failed the dashboard renders RoleLookupFailedView ('Couldn't verify your access' plus Retry) fail-closed before any data loads, instead of letting a real trainer whose lookup failed fall through to the office dashboard, and ?role= may only switch the displayed variant — it can never override the trainer redirect.

The sync-failed banner is SyncFailedCallout in modules/batches/ui/dashboard/DashboardCallouts.tsx: a warning InfoCallout with fixed copy 'Sync with Supabase failed — showing the last cached snapshot{ from <stamp>}' claimed only when isShowingCachedFallback (the rows actually came from a non-ok snapshot), otherwise '…showing the currently loaded data' — so a ?state=sync-failed preview over live rows does not claim cached provenance — ending with a Retry link; DashboardCallouts composes it in fixed order with the critical-docs callout, and the dashboard layout additionally suppresses MetricsRow whenever the snapshot is sync-failed, so the shell never renders derived metrics over a failed fetch.

The dashboard is the only route with a route-level loading.tsx (TES-8): a Suspense fallback that mirrors the real layout — page head with 'Loading latest snapshot…', six KPI blocks, charts row, and wide panels — marked aria-busy with the label 'Loading dashboard' and shaded from the shared surface/border tokens; elsewhere server fetches render once, so DESIGN.md 12's write-back loading treatments (.btn.loading spinner, aria-busy) apply to client islands and pending actions.
